terms.register: vōx plērumque poētica: Verg., Hor. (Lewis & Short)
evidence: Verg. G. 4.133: dapibus mēnsās onerābat inēmptīs
terms.comment: The Roman way of praising food from one’s own house and land was to call it “unbought”. In plain talk, say what was done at home: domī coctus, domī factus (see the examples).

phrases.latin: Hic pānis domī coctus est, nōn ēmptus.
phrases.english: This bread is home-made, not shop-bought.

phrases.latin: rēgum aequābat opēs animīs, sērāque revertēns nocte domum dapibus mēnsās onerābat inēmptīs
phrases.english: in his own mind he was as rich as kings, and coming home late at night he would load his table with food he had not bought

phrases.latin: et certē bētam et pānem autopȳrum dē suō sibi
phrases.english: and of course beet, and wholemeal bread of his own baking
